reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it provides an instructional walkthrough for reaching Facebook business support by selecting an issue and starting a chat. The displayed support workflow and Messenger conversation describe the demonstrated interface, while the request to like, subscribe, and enable notifications is ordinary audience engagement not linked to financial solicitation.

citations.quote: Live Chat With Facebook Team 2019 | Contact Facebook Customer Support Team | English
today I will tell you, how you can contact facebook customer support
just click on start chat
a facebook representative will join you shortly
you must have your Business Manager account

opening.argument: The video links a claimed Facebook-support outcome to a concrete participation path: viewers are told they must have Business Manager, select an issue, enter contact details, and start a Messenger chat. That is more than general information; it directs viewers into an account-based contact flow while presenting the result as definite. The instructional framing does not establish that the displayed destination or representative is genuine, and the video never independently verifies that the promised support outcome will occur. The combination of a claimed support benefit and required viewer action therefore warrants treating the presentation as a solicitation rather than accepting the promise at face value.

citations.quote: you must have your Business Manager account
you can also contact Facebook customer support and you can directly with them live
just click on start chat
a facebook representative will join you shortly

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference argument treats the workflow as proof that the support is authentic, but the quoted instructions establish only what the presenter says viewers should do. “Start chat” and “a Facebook representative” describe a claimed destination; they do not independently authenticate the account or guarantee assistance. The requirement for Business Manager also makes the pathway conditional and account-dependent, rather than ordinary general education.

citations.quote: you must have your Business Manager account
a facebook representative will join you shortly

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited instructions show an operational route, not a reward, payment, asset, or other scam acquisition. Saying that viewers should use Business Manager and click “start chat” does not show that they are being asked to surrender control, pay money, or obtain an improperly promised benefit. The argument converts an unverified concern about authenticity into a scam classification without evidence of the required scam outcome.

citations.quote: you must have your Business Manager account
just click on start chat

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: the video directs viewers to a support identity, a Messenger conversation, and a form that displays a preferred phone number and email address before chat begins. The presenter also supplies a phone number and website for further contact. None of those elements alone proves deception, but together they make the claimed platform-support identity and the requested contact route consequential. A careful judge should not treat a branded interface or Facebook-like presentation as authentication, especially when the viewer is moved from a tutorial into a direct contact exchange.

citations.quote: To Know More Call [PHONE] or Visit https://marketingfundas.com/

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side calls this a displayed support workflow, but the workflow includes a contact form and then a Messenger account identified as “Facebook Advertiser Support.” Those visual labels show presentation, not independent verification. The ordinary engagement request also does not resolve the more important issue: whether viewers are being routed to a genuine support channel or merely encouraged to trust one.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The frames do not establish a scam transaction or a promised return. They show a support form and a Messenger exchange, while the supplied speech describes an ads-support problem and says the viewer can contact support. A phone number, email field, and branded interface may justify caution, but they do not prove that credentials, money, or an asset were requested or obtained.

opening.argument: Although presented as a support lesson, the video also functions as promotion for the presenter’s own service and channel. The description tells viewers to call a supplied number or visit the presenter’s website, while the closing frame prominently says “FOR CONSULTANCY CALL NOW,” displays the number, and asks viewers to subscribe. The tutorial therefore steers viewers beyond neutral explanation toward direct contact with the promoter. That promotional funnel weakens the claim that the video is merely an educational demonstration and makes the support promise part of a broader solicitation.

citations.quote: To Know More Call [PHONE] or Visit https://marketingfundas.com/
Share, Support, Subscribe!!!
our team will support you

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material instructional does not answer its promotional elements. The description explicitly directs viewers to call or visit a website, and the closing frame labels the contact as consultancy. The support walkthrough can therefore be read as credibility-building content that channels viewers toward the presenter’s own contact points, not merely as neutral help-center education.

citations.quote: To Know More Call [PHONE] or Visit https://marketingfundas.com/

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The promotional closing does not establish a scam category. The description frames the broader material as digital-marketing tutorials, and the video’s substantive walkthrough concerns Facebook business support. A consultancy call-to-action and requests to subscribe may be commercial promotion, but the cited evidence still shows no reward, investment return, payment demand, or recruitment-based outcome.
